title: The Pound sells its own inflation spike ahead of a Fed hike
summary: The Pound trades just above 1.3450, down 23 pips, after a morning that ran in two directions. It climbed into the August inflation release at 06:00 GMT, spiked on it, then spent six hours handing the move back and another 30 pips with it.

title: Dow Jones Industrial Average huddles ahead of Fed action
summary: The Dow Jones Industrial Average trades just above 52,100 and has spent the Wednesday morning going nowhere, on the day the Federal Reserve (Fed) is expected to raise its rate for the first time since 2023. That is not indifference.

title: US Dollar: Fed repricing risk caps downside – Rabobank
summary: Rabobank’s Senior FX Strategist Jane Foley notes the US Dollar (USD) has outperformed G10 peers on expectations the Fed will deliver around 100 bps of tightening over 12 months, but warns this may be excessive.

title: Energy Shock Puts Bank of England Under Pressure to Raise Rates
summary: The Bank of England is facing mounting pressure to raise interest rates on Thursday amid a global bond market rout fuelled by concerns over runaway government borrowing and sticky inflation. Investors told Threadneedle Street it was “essential” to rein in prices before the energy shock triggered by the Iran war spreads through the economy and that failing to do so would risk the Bank “losing credibility”. title: Russia Extends Diesel Export Ban Through October
summary: Russia will extend its ban on diesel exports for all fuel producers to October 31, Vedomosti reported Tuesday, citing delayed refinery maintenance and the need to rebuild fuel reserves before winter. The ban, expanded in July from traders and small refineries to cover all producers, had been due to expire September 30. Diesel on the St. Petersburg commodity exchange traded at 70,546 rubles a ton in early September, and retail prices reached 88.44 rubles a liter on September 7, up 18.4% since the start of the year. title: TTF Gas Hits $92.95 as Gulf Tensions Weigh on Energy Markets
summary: Europe’s benchmark natural gas prices held above the 80-euro mark early on Wednesday, staying close to 2022 highs, as low gas volumes in storage sites fuel concerns about winter supplies amid continued disruption and widening conflict in the Middle East. The front-month price at the Dutch Title Transfer Facility (TTF), the benchmark for Europe’s gas trading, rose by 0.3% to $$92.95 (80.545 euros) per megawatt-hour (MWh) as of 9:15 a.m. in Amsterdam on Wednesday.
